thread:
alex: quick update — ran a run comparing fp8 vs int8 vs 4bit kernels on Mistral-7B and Qwen-7B with our latest kvcache batching heuristics. short summary: int8 calibrated gives slightly worse perplexity on long-context (>=2048) but is ~1.6x faster than fp8 in our env. fp8 still wins on latency for shorter seqs.

maya: can you paste the perf numbers and the profile flame graphs? curious about kernel-switch overheads

alex: paste below. these are p50 token ms measured on a dedicated A100 pool, batch=1/4/8, seq=512/1024/4096. model=Mistral-7B/qwen-7B. fp8: p50=[3.2/3.5/6.8] ms @ batch1, int8-calib: [2.0/2.4/5.5], 4bit: [1.9/2.1/5.9]. note 4bit has worse variance at 4096.

derek: interesting — where is the kv cache hit amplification? does cached prefix reduce kernel time proportionally?

alex: yes, when kvcache hit ratio >0.7 we see ~20-30% lower per-token times across all precisions because attention reduces to smaller matmuls. but int8 quantization introduces extra dequant steps which hurt when we have many small KV matmuls (i.e., long-context + small batch).

sara: did you try the hybrid routing we talked about? route long-context to fp8 and short-context to int8, with automatic fallback when latency SLO violated

alex: tried hybrid routing in canary. rule: if seq_len>2048 route fp8, else int8. reduced tail latency (p95) by ~15% for low concurrency customers, but increased cost ~8% due to fp8 token spend. quality-wise, int8-calib had a small drop on long context QA tests — ~1.8% F1 drop vs fp8.

maya: calibration details? how are we calibrating int8 for Mistral vs Qwen? different ranges?

alex: used per-channel minmax + KL divergence hist matching on 1k doc sample from eval corpus. Mistral needed narrower clip (0.98 percentile), Qwen required 0.995 to avoid quality hit. also layernorm layers suffer more in Qwen — we left them at fp16 in mixed-precision runs.

derek: kernel selection overhead: did you see expensive recompile when switching kernels per-request? that was a regression earlier.

alex: turned off on-the-fly kernel JIT in runtime for canary; we preselect kernel per model+quant_profile+device and cache it. eliminated the recompile stalls. perf-bot: deploy note — kernel-cache warmed after 30k tokens for canary cluster.

perf-bot: perf-regression-monitor: alert suppressed — canary stable, 4 warnings about variance in 4bit at high seq lengths

sara: can we surface config snippets for teams? a short example for hybrid routing + model profile

alex: snippet below:
```
model_profiles:
  - model: mistral-7b
    quant: int8-calib-2026-03
    fallback_quant: fp8-v2
    kv_cache_optim: true
    route:
      - if: seq_len > 2048
        quant: fp8-v2
      - else: int8-calib-2026-03
```

maya: can you drop the calibration artifacts and the tiny eval log? I'll put in the model-profiles repo

alex: pushing to /repos/model-profiles/mistral/qwen/ later today. will include the eval prompts, calibration histograms, and perf traces.

derek: one more ask — add a knob in Optimize UI to suggest hybrid routing when int8 calibration loss > threshold

sara: yes please. file an issue — tag eng-runtime/console. :thumbsup:
